record.paper_title: Fluctuation Limit of Branching Processes with Immigration and Estimation of the Means
record.context_brief: Optimal Lindeberg conditions for fluctuation limits
record.original_question: Consider a triangular sequence of Galton-Watson branching processes with immigration X_k^(n), started from X_0^(n)=0, where the offspring mean m_n satisfies m_n = 1 + alpha/n + o(1/n), the offspring variance sigma_n^2 satisfies sigma_n^2 = beta/n + o(1/n), the immigration mean lambda_n tends to lambda, and the immigration variance b_n^2 tends to b^2. The centered martingale increments are M_k^(n)=X_k^(n)-m_n X_{k-1}^(n)-lambda_n, and the fluctuation theorem studies weak convergence of n^{-1/2}(X^(n)-E X^(n), M^(n)) in Skorokhod space. Are the Lindeberg conditions imposed separately on the normalized offspring variables (xi_{k,j}^{(n)}-m_n)/sqrt(n) and immigration variables (epsilon_k^(n)-lambda_n)/sqrt(n) necessary and sufficient for that fluctuation convergence, or can they be replaced by strictly weaker distributional assumptions?

evidence.quote: Conditions (iii) and (v) are, in fact, the Lindeberg conditions for the triangular systems {ξ (n) k,j /n1/2 : n ∈ N, 1 ≤ k, j ≤ n} and {ε (n) j /n1/2 : n ∈ N, 1 ≤ j ≤ n}, respectively; see also Grimvall [4], who investigated fluctuation theorems for sequences of branching processes without immigration, and the remarks in the introduction.
This suggests that our Lindeberg-type conditions on the offspring and immigration distributions are close to being optimal.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each integer $n\ge 1$, let $\{\xi^{(n)}_{k,j}: k,j\ge 1\}$ be i.i.d. nonnegative integer-valued random variables (offspring distribution) with mean $m_n$ and variance $\sigma_n^2$, and independently let $\{\varepsilon^{(n)}_k: k\ge 1\}$ be i.i.d. nonnegative integer-valued random variables (immigration distribution) with mean $\lambda_n$ and variance $b_n^2$. Define the Galton–Watson process with immigration $\{X^{(n)}_k: k\ge 0\}$ by $X^{(n)}_0=0$ and
$$X^{(n)}_k \;=\; \sum_{j=1}^{X^{(n)}_{k-1}}\xi^{(n)}_{k,j} \;+\; \varepsilon^{(n)}_k, \qquad k\ge 1,$$
and the martingale increments $M^{(n)}_k = X^{(n)}_k - m_n X^{(n)}_{k-1} - \lambda_n$. Assume the nearly critical regime
$$m_n = 1 + \frac{\alpha}{n} + o(1/n), \qquad \sigma_n^2 = \frac{\beta}{n} + o(1/n), \qquad \lambda_n\to\lambda, \qquad b_n^2\to b^2,$$
with $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$ and $\beta,\lambda,b^2\ge 0$. Consider the rescaled càdlàg processes
$$\bigl(\,n^{-1/2}(X^{(n)}_{\lfloor nt\rfloor}-\mathbb{E}X^{(n)}_{\lfloor nt\rfloor}),\; n^{-1/2}\textstyle\sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor nt\rfloor}M^{(n)}_k\bigr)_{t\ge 0}$$
in the Skorokhod space $D(\mathbb{R}_+,\mathbb{R}^2)$. Consider the two Lindeberg-type conditions on the triangular arrays
$$\text{(L1)}\quad \sum_{k,j=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}\!\left[\frac{(\xi^{(n)}_{k,j}-m_n)^2}{n}\,\mathbf{1}_{\{|\xi^{(n)}_{k,j}-m_n|>\eta\sqrt{n}\}}\right]\to 0,\qquad \forall\,\eta>0,$$
$$\text{(L2)}\quad \sum_{k=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}\!\left[\frac{(\varepsilon^{(n)}_k-\lambda_n)^2}{n}\,\mathbf{1}_{\{|\varepsilon^{(n)}_k-\lambda_n|>\eta\sqrt{n}\}}\right]\to 0,\qquad \forall\,\eta>0.$$
It is known that under the moment regime above together with (L1) and (L2), the rescaled processes converge weakly in $D(\mathbb{R}_+,\mathbb{R}^2)$ to an explicit Gaussian/Ornstein–Uhlenbeck-type limit. Question: are conditions (L1) and (L2) necessary as well as sufficient for this fluctuation convergence, or can they be replaced by strictly weaker distributional conditions on the offspring and immigration laws?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search located the work establishing the fluctuation theorem under the stated Lindeberg-type conditions and follow-up surveys on nearly critical Galton–Watson processes with immigration, but no source was found that proves the necessity of (L1) and (L2) or replaces them with strictly weaker conditions. The optimality question therefore appears unresolved in the literature reachable by search.

status_evidence.title: Fluctuation limit of branching processes with immigration and estimation of the means
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes fluctuation theorem under Lindeberg-type conditions on offspring and immigration triangular arrays.
status_evidence.claim: Source providing the sufficient Lindeberg conditions whose optimality is in question.

status_evidence.title: Critical branching processes with immigration (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of functional limit theorems for nearly critical Galton–Watson processes with immigration via martingale methods.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent survey does not report a strengthening removing or weakening the Lindeberg conditions.
